original_question: Fix an integer Delta >= 3 and let G be a connected nonregular graph on n vertices with maximum spectral radius among all connected nonregular graphs with maximum degree Delta. Does the limit of n^2(Delta - lambda(G))/(Delta - 1) always exist when Delta is odd and equal pi^2/4, and when Delta is even does the limit of n^2(Delta - lambda(G))/(Delta - 2) always exist and equal pi^2/2?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 10 (Liu [103]) in the survey’s topic on the extremal spectral radius of connected nonregular graphs with prescribed maximum degree.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper-faithful target. It correctly fixes an integer Δ ≥ 3, considers connected nonregular graphs on n vertices with maximum degree Δ that maximize spectral radius, and captures the parity split and the exact constants π^2/4 and π^2/2 with the normalizing factors Δ-1 and Δ-2. That matches the content of Conjecture 10 in the paper.
missing_details: The paper’s notation should be made explicit: λ(G) means the adjacency spectral radius, i.e. the largest eigenvalue λ1(A(G)) of the adjacency matrix of a simple, undirected graph G.
Because n tends to infinity, one should not speak of a single fixed graph G; formally one needs a sequence G_n in the extremal family, or equivalently the scalar extremal value λ(n,Δ).
The extremal class should be specified as all connected, nonregular graphs on exactly n vertices with maximum degree exactly Δ, not merely graphs with maximum degree bounded by Δ.
The paper introduces 𝒢(n,Δ) for the set of extremal graphs and λ(n,Δ) for their common maximum spectral radius; using this notation removes ambiguity when the extremal graph is not unique.
The official formulation first asks whether the limit of n^2(Δ-λ(G)) exists at all, and then states the predicted parity-dependent normalized values; your draft only states the normalized limits.
It should be explicit that Δ is fixed while n → ∞.
If one phrases the question using G rather than λ(n,Δ), one should note that the limit is well defined because every G in 𝒢(n,Δ) has the same spectral radius by definition.

The relevant parity in this conjecture is the parity of Δ; this should be kept distinct from the parity condition nΔ odd/even that appears in a different conjecture about the degree sequence of extremal graphs.
refined_question:
For a fixed integer Δ ≥ 3, let 𝒢(n,Δ) be the set of all connected, simple, undirected, nonregular graphs on n vertices with maximum degree exactly Δ that attain the maximum adjacency spectral radius among all such graphs, and let λ(G)=λ1(A(G)) denote the spectral radius of G. If G_n ∈ 𝒢(n,Δ) for each n, does the limit of n^2(Δ-λ(G_n)) exist as n → ∞? More precisely, is it true that
(1) if Δ is odd, then lim_{n→∞} n^2(Δ-λ(G_n))/(Δ-1)=π^2/4; and
(2) if Δ is even, then lim_{n→∞} n^2(Δ-λ(G_n))/(Δ-2)=π^2/2?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, writing λ(n,Δ):=max{λ(H): H is a connected, simple, undirected, nonregular graph on n vertices with maximum degree Δ}, is it true that for every fixed integer Δ ≥ 3 the limit of n^2(Δ-λ(n,Δ)) exists, and moreover equals (Δ-1)π^2/4 when Δ is odd and (Δ-2)π^2/2 when Δ is even?
justification: The draft is not aiming at the earlier Liu-Shen-Wang conjecture with limit π^2 and denominator Δ-1 for every fixed Δ. Rather, it matches the later replacement conjecture stated in this survey after the paper explains that the earlier conjecture was disproved by Liu [103]. The parity-dependent normalizations and constants in your draft agree exactly with Conjecture 10. The nearby context on the same page introduces the extremal notation 𝒢(n,Δ) and λ(n,Δ), explains that Liu [103] gave a negative answer to the older conjecture, and then presents this sharper parity-sensitive conjecture. The introduction of the survey supplies the ambient graph model and the meaning of λ(G).
